name: Monster Cookies

ingredients.name: creamy emulsified peanut butter, such as Jif
M&M’s Minis, plus more for decoration, if desired

instructions.primary_message: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, cream together butter, sugar, baking soda, and salt on medium speed until mixture is light, fluffy, and pale, about 4 minutes. Alternatively, use an electric hand mixer.

Add peanut butter and vanilla extract and beat on medium until smooth and fully incorporated, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed, about 1 minute. Add eggs one at a time, beating on medium until just incorporated. Add all-purpose flour and mix on low speed until barely combined, with some dry flour still remaining, about 15 seconds. Add rolled oats and mix on low speed until incorporated, about 15 seconds longer.
With a rubber spatula, fold in chocolate and M&M’s. Turn dough out onto a sheet of plastic wrap, wrap tightly, and refrigerate for at least one hour and up to 24 hours.

Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Line 2 rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper. Portion dough into sixteen 56 g balls (about 1/4 cup each) and roll into smooth balls. Place 6 dough balls at least 8 cm apart on 1 prepared baking sheet. If desired for visual effect, press 3 to 4 additional mini M&M’s into the top of each cookie.

Bake until edges are golden brown but centers are still soft, 13 to 15 minutes. For perfectly circular cookies, immediately invert a round plastic quart container (or a glass or bowl about 10 to 13 cm in diameter) over each cookie and rapidly swirl it around the cookie, gently bumping the soft edges into a neat circle. Let cookies cool on baking sheet for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. Repeat portioning, shaping, and baking with remaining dough.

description: These soft and chewy monster cookies are packed with peanut butter, rolled oats, chopped chocolate, and mini M&M’s for a little of everything in every bite.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 25 min.

Notes: An equal amount by weight of oat flour or rolled oats pulverized in a blender or food processor can be substituted for the all-purpose flour to make these cookies gluten-free (do not substitute whole rolled oats). The freshly mixed dough will be especially soft and sticky; chill overnight if possible. (While oats are naturally gluten-free, they can be cross-contaminated when they are grown or processed alongside grains such as wheat and barley that contain gluten. If gluten is a concern, be sure to use oats labeled gluten-free.)

Make-ahead and storage: Cookies can be stored at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 10 days.
author: Liz Cook
